dialogues.speaker: Jarry
dialogues.text: ...For goodness' sake, I'm not an adventurer or anything like that. I'm just picking up goods for someone. I'm out of there soon as the tunnel blasting's done.

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: But you know what the creepy thing is? They say that no one who has ventured into Ogurov has ever come back out...

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: And who in their right mind would have their goods there? What if this is all a setup? What if you get robbed by a bunch of hooligans the moment you get there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Excuse us, we're Paimon and {NICKNAME}. We're adventurers who travel the world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We heard you talking about some town called... um... Ogurovo or Oguro-voro or something. It's actually where we're headed!

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: Oh. Hello, my name is Vinezka. And this is Jarry, my fiancé.

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: Are you on an adventure to Ogurov? But it was abandoned a long time ago. And the train can't even get in there now.

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: But, I know of a few folks who are planning to go there to pick up some goods. They're the ones who hired my fiancé to blast open the tunnel for them.

dialogues.speaker: Jarry
dialogues.text: That's right. But Vinezka over here doesn't want me to go now, so I have no choice but to pay a hefty penalty now.

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: Hmph! I can't believe I'm actually getting blamed here. This is for your own good! Won't the two of you say something reasonable here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure. I'm always happy to be the voice of reason.

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: ...Back in the day, everyone used to say that Ogurov was a great place to be. The weather there was warm enough, and there even was a famous doctor there. At that time, moving to Ogurov seemed like the most natural thing to do.

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: But later on, someone realized that no one who has gone into Ogurov had ever come back out since...

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: There's a line from "Tales of the Strange From Ogurov" that reads, "Deep in a beautiful mountain valley lives a magnificent firebird, a bird so beautiful that it is impossible to look away from it..."

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: "Its wings, when spread, are so large they can blot out the sky; its eyes gleam like gemstones, while its feathers dazzle like gold. All who behold it cannot help themselves but follow it deep into the valley..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're saying, nobody can get out of that Ogurovo place or something because that firebird is so pretty?

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: No, that's not what I mean. They probably were eaten by that firebird.

dialogues.speaker: Jarry
dialogues.text: Oh, for goodness' sake, Vinezka. If that sort of monster really exists, would it have left Ogurov to eat everyone else by now? I've never seen a bird like that myself, that's for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: I don't care. You're not going in either case.

dialogues.speaker: Jarry
dialogues.text: Tsk. Then I'll have to get someone to go in my place at least...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... An abandoned town and a legend of a strange creature...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #(Hey, Goggles, {NICKNAME}. Do you guys think this might be related to the thing Goggles is looking for?)

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: ...Based on the description, it does appear that there is some kind of connection.

dialogues.speaker: Jarry
dialogues.text: *Sigh* But where can I find someone on such short notice???

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll do it! What is an adventurer, if not one who keeps adventuring?

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: Oh? How terribly kind of you! Looks like Jarry won't be going then... I wish you two a most fruitful adventure! Jarry and I will be praying for you!

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: They haven't come knocking yet... I've sold every piece of jewelry I could, but it still won't be enough to pay off the penalty.

dialogues.speaker: Jarry
dialogues.text: Maybe they've already done the job for me? Try to look on the bright side. At least nothing bad has happened yet.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hey there. How have you been?

dialogues.speaker: Jarry
dialogues.text: Wonderful! You look like you're doing well. Did you run into any trouble? Vinezka has been very worried about you two.

choices.text: There is indeed a Firebird in Okurov.

response.speaker: Vinezka
response.text: I knew it! Good thing you didn't go. With those skinny little arms and legs of yours, you wouldn't even make a mouthful for that thing!

response.speaker: Vinezka
response.text: Good thing we had this experienced adventurer take the job instead. Otherwise, forget earning the pay to buy me a ring. You might not have made it back at all!

response.speaker: Vinezka
response.text: Phew... Please take these. It's not much, but consider it our small token of thanks...

choices.text: There was a gang there trying to rob people...

response.speaker: Jarry
response.text: So Vinezka really was right... But seeing as you made it back safe and sound, I suppose you've already dealt with them?

response.speaker: Jarry
response.text: Phew, good thing I didn't go. Otherwise, I would've gone through all that for nothing... But does this mean we don't have to pay that penalty now?

response.speaker: Jarry
response.text: In that case, please take these. It's not much, but consider it our small token of thanks...

response.speaker: Vinezka
response.text: Now I can buy back my jewelry right away... No, I'll buy a whole new set!

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: They haven't come knocking yet... I've sold every piece of jewelry I could, but it still won't be enough to pay off the penalty.

dialogues.speaker: Jarry
dialogues.text: *sigh* I just wanted to buy you the best, shiniest ring there is... Or maybe I could go take a look by the tunnel entrance?

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: Absolutely not... The latest, latest issue of "Tales of the Strange From Ogurov" says that giant Firebird has started showing up again lately...

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: There's even a witness called "The Anvil" who claims he saw that giant Firebird swallow a whole section of a train car in one gulp!

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: You should stay away from the tunnel entrance, for your own safety.

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: If there's really, really no other way, we could hire a private detective to go and look into it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've already done the job for you.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Jarry about the tunnel being opened on the outskirts of Okurov...

dialogues.speaker: Jarry
dialogues.text: I see. So that's what happened... In other words, you've already done the job for me? You are mu savior! Please, take this little token of thanks...

dialogues.speaker: Vinezka
dialogues.text: Ah, then we won't have to pay the penalty either. I need to go buy back my jewelry right away... No, I'll buy a whole new set!

dialogues.speaker: Jarry
dialogues.text: I'm really worried they'll come for me...

response.speaker: Jarry
response.text: Well, yes, you're right, but I already signed the contract...

response.speaker: Jarry
response.text: Besides, I wouldn't know where to get the money to buy my fiancée a shiny wedding ring without this payment.

response.speaker: Vinezka
response.text: No ring is more important than your safety, no matter how shiny it is...

choices.text: I'll finish this job for you.

response.speaker: Vinezka
response.text: Anyway, I want to thank you on his behalf... Ever since I found out he took this job, I've been having trouble sleeping. I can finally be at ease tonight...

response.speaker: Vinezka
response.text: Of course, if they really come demanding a hundred-times penalty, I'll bear it with him. That's still better than him putting himself in danger.
